meta.title: Plan gates don't converge. Code gates do.
meta.verdict: 4 rounds, 8-7-8-7 flat. Every plan chain in this repo: 0 for 4. Every code chain: 1 for 1.
meta.lede: The gate was not made stricter by design. On 2026-07-09 its reviewer moved to the ultra effort tier, which silently spawns ~3 sub-reviewers every round and copies the entire growing history into each. Under a zero-blocker approval rule, that is a loop that cannot terminate — and the model family is not what separates the eras. The effort dial is.

ask.headline: One call is open tonight: keep gating the Wave 2a plan, or change the artifact class and gate the code instead?
ask.note: Three further owner calls — fast-mode spend, the 2-defect recall loss, and which runtime is authoritative — are queued in the plan below.
ask.recommendation: A — build the manifest, gate the CODE
ask.recommendedBy: Claude — on the repo's own convergence record, and it is #31's remedy applied to #31's own successor

items.title: ROOT CAUSE — the 'ultra' effort dial, not sol-vs-terra
items.evidence: spawn_agent calls by reviewer pair: gpt-5.5@xhigh 0 across 639 threads; gpt-5.6-sol@HIGH 0 across 3 threads; gpt-5.6-sol@ultra 988 across 1,147; gpt-5.6-terra@ultra 72 across 68. The sol@high row is the decisive natural control — same model family, non-ultra effort, zero delegation.

items.title: 'ultra' silently turns a single-lens gate into a ~3-child ensemble
items.evidence: Codex's model cache defines ultra as 'Maximum reasoning with automatic task delegation'. Traces show ~3 auto-spawned reviewers per nominal round (impl_audit / contract_audit / test_audit), created by the MODEL — not by the wrapper. CODEX_GATE_FANOUT and --multi do not bound them.

items.title: Children inherit fork_turns=all, so each round re-copies a growing history
items.evidence: 3,508 fork_turns occurrences under sol@ultra, 250 under terra@ultra, 0 under gpt-5.5@xhigh. A Steward round-1 child received ~50.8k user-message chars; the round-5 child received 609k — every packet plus prior root replies. Cost and latency grow superlinearly per round.

items.title: Changepoint is 2026-07-09 — the day the pair changed to sol@ultra
items.evidence: gpt-5.5@xhigh on every run through Jul 8; sol@ultra from Jul 9; terra@ultra from Aug 10. Effort was xhigh on 100% of gpt-5.5 runs and ultra on 100% of sol/terra runs, so observational data alone cannot split model from effort — the spawn counts above are what split it.

items.title: Approve rate collapsed 36% to 0%; blockers per round rose 1 to 13
items.evidence: gpt-5.5@xhigh: 657 rounds, median 1 blocker, 35.6% approve. sol@ultra: 215 rounds, median 5, 4.7% approve. terra@ultra: 14 rounds, median 13, 0% approve.

items.title: Holds under three independent mode controls — not a work-mix artifact
items.evidence: prepr (same task shape throughout): 1.2 to 6.6 mean blockers, 31.5% to 1.2% approve. bundle: 2.1 to 14.2, 27.5% to 0%. phase: 1.2 to 7.8, 34.2% to 0%. Every mode steps the same way at the same date.

items.title: Convergence per review chain fell 77% to 19% to 0%
items.evidence: 282 chains under gpt-5.5 reached approve 77% of the time (median 2 rounds). 54 chains under sol: 19%. 6 chains under terra: 0%. Longest chain rose from 19 rounds to 34.

items.title: Severity inflated, not just volume: P1s per round went 0.75 to 9.6
items.evidence: Per-round means — P1: 0.75 / 3.24 / 9.57 across the three eras. Decision-class blockers (the ones that cannot be auto-fixed and force an owner stop): 0.04 / 0.32 / 1.64, a 40x rise.

items.title: Latency rose 5x — median round 154s to 815s, p90 to 6,623s
items.evidence: Median wall-clock per round: 154s (gpt-5.5) to 632s (sol) to 815s (terra). This is the literal 'slowing things down'. Duration is a file-mtime proxy, so medians are trustworthy but individual outliers are not.

items.title: Fast-mode OFF (Aug 10) is a real but SECONDARY latency contributor
items.evidence: Shipped v1.1.0 pins CODEX_GATE_FAST=1; the live skill pins 0. But per-round wall time is broadly similar across the fast-ON sol era and fast-OFF terra era (12.5-15.1 min), so hidden fan-out x repeated rounds dominates, not fast mode. Not isolated by existing data.

items.title: The 8-round cap is prose only — the wrapper never enforces it
items.evidence: CODEX_GATE_MAX_ROUNDS occurs 3x in SKILL.md and 0x in codex-gate.sh. Nothing computes blocker fingerprints, trend, or introduced-by-fix relationships, so a driver can reach 13 rounds against a documented backstop of 8.

items.title: Issue #31's 'the code gate converged' claim is factually wrong
items.evidence: Cartographer Phase 1 raw verdicts were 15 -> 5 -> 11 -> 5, ALL request_changes. It never reached APPROVE; it stopped on owner judgement with five recorded residuals. The issue should be narrowed to 'code review started lower and produced more executable evidence'.

items.title: Issues #30 and #31 describe real doctrine gaps but misattribute the trigger
items.evidence: The same doctrine converged 77% of chains before Jul 9. The doctrine gaps (no trend guard, no legal exits, unscoped phase review, no subtraction pressure) are worth closing on their own merits, but they are amplifiers — the trigger is the effort dial.

items.title: Two independent minings agree exactly on the bundle-mode split
items.evidence: This analysis and the separate Codex investigation, run with different methods, both found 102 pre-Jul-9 bundle verdicts with 28 APPROVE, and 47 post-switch bundle verdicts with 0 APPROVE. Spawn totals differ slightly (988 vs 693) only because of gate-thread vs all-rollout counting.

findings.summary: The gate was not made stricter by design — on 2026-07-09 its reviewer moved to 'ultra', an effort tier that automatically spawns ~3 sub-reviewers per round and forks the entire growing history into each. Zero spawns in 639 gpt-5.5@xhigh threads and zero in 3 sol@high threads; 1,060 under ultra. That ensemble finds a fresh crop of real-but-ever-remoter defects every round, which under a zero-blocker approval rule is a loop that cannot terminate. Model family (sol vs terra) is not the discriminator; the effort dial is.

liveRun.what: Frozen-packet effort sweep, per the Codex investigation's P0 recommendation. ONE frozen copy of the-cartographer bundle (1,861 lines), reviewed by codex-gate under a fresh root thread per cell — no resume across variants, fast mode held OFF throughout so it cannot confound. Core arms: terra@ultra (current default, control), terra@max, terra@xhigh. Optional extension: sol@max, sol@ultra (same-packet model-family comparison) and gpt-5.5@xhigh (the known-good pre-Jul-9 anchor). Per arm we record auto-spawned subagent count and task names, active wall time, token totals, and blocker count by severity and class.
liveRun.cost: One bundle round per arm at the tier the gate already runs daily: 3 arms is roughly 25-45 min, 6 arms roughly 60-100 min (the xhigh/max arms should be materially faster than ultra if the fan-out hypothesis holds). Codex credits only; no Anthropic spend. A phase-review P2 gate is running right now at terra@ultra, so arms are queued behind it rather than run concurrently.
liveRun.blastRadius: Read-only. codex-gate invokes Codex with --sandbox read-only, approval_policy=never and a config-isolated CODEX_HOME, so it cannot write to the repo. Only new directories under ~/.claude/codex-gate/runs/<experiment-session>/ are written. No repo mutation, no branch, no commit, no push, no PR, nothing sent externally, no GitHub issue touched. Model and effort are passed per invocation via env for the experiment only — the committed defaults in codex-gate.sh are NOT edited, so this decides nothing on its own.
liveRun.cleanup: All arms land under one experiment session slug; deleting that one directory removes everything. The running P2 gate is left strictly alone — no shared round paths, no signals sent to it. Verdict JSONs are retained as the evidence base for the remedy decision that follows.

slides.statement: The gate stopped helping and started costing
slides.lead: It turned on 2026-07-09 — and the ultra effort dial is the culprit, not the model.
bullets: Your read was right that it began with a model-default change — the date is **2026-07-09**, earlier than the Aug 10 terra switch.
But the model family is not the culprit. The **`ultra` effort dial** is.
Two independent investigations plus a 6-arm controlled sweep agree.

bullets: Codex's model catalog defines `ultra` as *Maximum reasoning with automatic task delegation*.
It spawns ~3 sub-reviewers per round, each inheriting `fork_turns=all` — every round re-copies a growing history.
**Three is a capped floor, not a ceiling:** descendants attempted further nested delegation and hit the global thread limit.
The wrapper's own fan-out controls (`--multi`, `CODEX_GATE_FANOUT`) do not bound them.

slides.heading: Only 4 of ~13 findings are about code at all
slides.statement: Only 4 of ~13 findings are about code at all
slides.lead: Every fix adds prose, and prose adds surface.
bullets: The rest are findings about the plan documents — and 0–3 per arm about *handoff* docs.
`bundle` recursively ingests every `.md` under the initiative, so plan docs plus accumulated handoffs are ~70% of the surface.
Every fix adds more prose, which adds more surface. That is the non-termination engine.
**Correction:** lower-effort terra did NOT skip the code — it opened 9–10 `.mjs` files and simply reported fewer findings. A reporting threshold, not blindness.

slides.heading: What this evidence does NOT establish
slides.statement: What this evidence does NOT establish
slides.lead: One round per arm, single samples — and Wave 1 is not a convergence fix.
bullets: **Wave 1 is not a convergence fix.** Blocker volume was 11–15 in every arm regardless of model or effort. It does not close #30 or #31.
**One round per arm**, single sample, stochastic output — nothing here is variance-controlled.
**Round-1 only** — never measures rounds-to-convergence.
**Group A is uncontrolled**; cross-group comparison is invalid.

slides.heading: The plan bundle was gated and came back BLOCK
slides.statement: The plan bundle was gated and came back BLOCK
slides.lead: It even caught a real bug in codex-gate itself.
bullets: 9 blockers: 6 agent-fixable (now folded in), 3 decision-class (yours, below).

It caught a real bug in codex-gate itself: `CODEX_GATE_MODEL=""` cannot fall through to Codex's default, because `${VAR:-…}` treats empty as unset. The documented escape hatch has never worked and the `-n` guard at `:576` is dead code.
It caught that my fan-out guard covered only `--multi`, missing the `CODEX_GATE_FANOUT=1` path at `codex-gate.sh:1425`.
One finding I rejected: it said `bundle_sha` was blank — the blank column is `packet_sha`. The provenance gap underneath was real and is closed.

decision.question: Wave 2a's plan gate is flat at 4 rounds after two subtractions, and the remaining findings are specification refinements of a specification. Change the artifact class rather than the scope?

options.label: A — build the manifest, gate the CODE
options.pros: This is issue #31's own remedy, and we now have direct evidence it works: Wave 1's code diff reached APPROVE in 2 rounds with 9/9 coverage, while every plan bundle in this repo (13, 5, 6, and now 4 rounds) never converged. Most of the open findings are ANSWERED by implementation rather than prose — symlinked manifest topology, path basis, locale-safe whitespace and deterministic ordering all become concrete and testable the moment there is code. The 7 findings become the implementation spec.
options.cons: Deviates from the-foreman's rule that the plan bundle reaches APPROVE before implementation. That is a governance gate, so it is your call to waive, not mine. Risk: building against an unapproved plan can bake in a design flaw that prose review would have caught cheaply — which is exactly what happened with the round model.

options.label: B — fold round 5 and keep gating the plan
options.pros: Six of seven are agent-fixable and genuinely small; decision-class dropped 3 -> 1, which is the one metric that IS improving.
options.cons: Four rounds of evidence say the count does not fall. Each fix adds prose, and prose adds surface. This is the loop #30 describes, chosen knowingly for a fifth round.

options.label: C — cut to a spike: manifest with no status contract
options.pros: Smallest possible executable slice — read the manifest, use it for both enumeration sites, no bundlePacket, no omitted[], no status shape. Nearly all seven findings are about the STATUS contract, not the selection logic. Ship selection, learn from it, add reporting later.
options.cons: Loses R2 (omission visibility) entirely, which was the whole safety argument for a manifest — a silently smaller packet is worse than a wildcard one.

options.label: D — stop Wave 2 here for tonight
options.pros: Wave 1 is approved. The round-model diagnosis is captured. The plan-vs-code convergence table is a genuine finding worth writing up on its own.

decision.recommendation: A — build the manifest, gate the CODE
